title: Tanzanian Fresh Oysters
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Oysters — Zanzibar tidal flat oysters shucked fresh and served on the half-shell with lemon juice, pili pili, and a ginger-lime dressing. The ultimate Zanzibar luxury at the world's best price — fresh from the tidal flats to the table.
longDesc: Zanzibar oysters collected from tidal rocks by local women and sold at the waterfront markets — extraordinary quality, briny, sweet, and deeply of the Indian Ocean. Eaten raw at the water's edge with lemon and pili pili.
ingredients: Pili pili sauce on the side
steps: Keep oysters alive and cold until serving.
Make ginger-lime dressing: combine lime, ginger, honey, and salt.
Prepare a large platter of crushed ice.
Shuck oysters: hold with cloth. Insert knife at hinge. Twist. Pop lid. Slide knife under to cut muscle.
Place on crushed ice cup-side down.
Add a few drops of dressing to each.
Serve with pili pili on the side.
chefTips: Oysters must be alive — discard any already open.
The liquor inside is the most flavourful part — do not lose it.
cookingScience: Raw oysters are eaten alive — only safe from sustainably harvested clean waters. Zanzibar's tidal flat oysters come from waters harvested without industrial contamination for centuries.
sustainabilityTips: Zanzibar tidal flat oysters — harvested by hand, no bycatch, filter feeding that cleans the water.
servedWith: Cold White Wine or Lime Juice
storage: Live oysters refrigerate 1—2 days. Eat immediately after shucking.
culturalNote: Zanzibar oysters eaten at the tidal flat, just shucked, with lime and pili pili — one of the world's great simple pleasures, shared by locals and visitors alike.
